name: MA-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+11 district with an incumbent Democrat running

model.rationale: Jake Auchincloss holds a district that leans eleven points Democratic, enjoys the advantages of incumbency, and has out-raised Thomas Stalcup by more than a hundred to one in cash on hand. Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 97 percent, and nothing in the record suggests the challenger has resources or visibility to close that gap.
model.watch: Any independent polling showing a single-digit race, or an outside-spending surge behind the Republican challenger, would be the first sign this is moving off safe.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jake Auchincloss, a Democratic incumbent, defends a Massachusetts district that leans eleven points Democratic. No general-election polling exists for this race, but the underlying fundamentals point strongly his way: he has raised over $3.6 million and holds $7.3 million in cash on hand, while Republican Thomas Stalcup has raised roughly $26,000 with about $1,300 available. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance at 97 percent.

The district's partisan lean, Auchincloss's incumbency, and the enormous resource gap leave the challenger without a visible path to competitiveness. Barring an external shock, this seat is expected to remain Democratic by a wide margin, placing it firmly in the safe Democratic category for the fall.
